ei.title: The Subscription Economy: From Ownership to Access
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: Jiyun, a high school student, starts her day by logging in to a music streaming service on her smartphone. She enjoys listening to her favorite music, discovering new songs, and exploring new artists every day. For a healthy breakfast, Jiyun receives a delivery from a subscription service that provides fresh vegetables and fruits. After school, Jiyun utilizes a video lecture service to expand her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting. For example, she watches various academic lectures to review her schoolwork and stay updated about the latest knowledge in her chosen field of study. During weekends, Jiyun and her family spend quality time together watching movies or dramas using a streaming service. Subscriptions are everywhere To be sure, the subscription economy is a popular economic model nowadays, and Jiyun is actively taking part in it. The concept of business models based on subscriptions is not new. Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers. However, these business models have expanded to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more. Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now prioritize providing continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates. Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription. The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers. Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model. From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences. They can also save money by having flexible subscription contracts. The rise of the subscription economy is closely connected to two major drivers: changes in consumption trends and the rapid growth of online platforms. People love the subscriptions The subscription economy is highly relevant to how people consume goods and services nowadays. More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things. This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership. For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums. Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers. Moreover, consumers value diversity and customization. The subscription economy offers a diverse range of subscription options, enabling individuals to personalize their experiences based on their own preferences and interests. This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes. A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service. It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns. To come to the point, consumers receive a personalized experience that prioritizes their individual skin conditions, rather than a uniform purchasing process. Furthermore, consumers appreciate flexibility and convenience. In some subscription models, consumers can experience a variety of products or services for a fixed cost. In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed. This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need. Moreover, subscription services are made easily accessible by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience. With just a few clicks, consumers can receive services or products. If they wish to change their device model, they can do so. Whoever desires an upgrade can get it and experience the latest models. Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices centered on smartphones, consumers have been able to do numerous things with great ease. In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos they wanted to watch. Today, whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms and enjoy a vast selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices. At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer customized products and services to customers. By applying AI and big data algorithm technology, companies identify consumers’ needs, tastes, and consumption patterns. People appreciate having diverse choices and customization, which in turn enhances their satisfaction. Services, such as suggesting personalized clothing styles based on customers’ purchase history or recommending videos that match their movie and video viewing history, bring them great satisfaction. Limitations of the subscription economy Although the subscription economy offers many advantages, there are also some disadvantages to consider. One concern is the potential for overconsumption. The convenience and accessibility of the subscription model make it easy for consumers to sign up for multiple services and use a lot of content or products. This can result in excessive consumption and using more subscription services than actually needed. It is crucial to subscribe only to services that are truly necessary and avoid subscribing to similar services. Related to the concern of overconsumption is the financial burden that subscriptions can create. While the cost of individual subscriptions may seem affordable, subscribing to multiple services can add up quickly. It is important to carefully consider the costs of these subscriptions to avoid financial strain. Regularly reviewing and canceling unnecessary subscriptions can be beneficial. Additionally, the subscription economy can contribute to environmental pollution. The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can increase the use of disposable packaging, which harms the environment. Using environmentally friendly packaging materials and opting for reusable packaging can help reduce this problem. Despite the potential limitations of subscription services, they have become deeply embedded in our lives and more and more businesses are jumping onto the subscription economy model. It is expected that new subscription services will be continuously provided to consumers in new areas in the future. We need to have a deeper understanding of the subscription economy and become wise consumers who receive the services that are really needed.

questions.passage: The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers. Companies can have a (A)[stable / unstable] revenue and build customer loyalty by using the subscription model. From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a (B)[wider / narrower] range of choices and personalized experiences. They can also save money by having (C)[flexible / rigid] subscription contracts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① narrower(더 좁은)·rigid(경직된)는 소비자 이점 문맥과 반대

✅ ② stable(안정적인)+wider(더 넓은)+flexible(유연한) ← 정답

❌ ③ unstable(불안정한)은 기업이 얻는 '안정적' 수익과 반대

❌ ④ 세 단어 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: stable revenue(안정적 수익), wider range(더 넓은 선택폭), flexible contracts(유연한 계약)

questions.passage: More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things. This makes the subscription economy (A)[attractive / unattractive] to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of ownership. For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy (B)[limitless / limited] music without the need for having disc albums. Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can (C)[explore / ignore] a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① unattractive(매력 없는)·limited(제한된)·ignore(무시하다)는 모두 문맥과 반대

❌ ② limited(제한된)는 '무제한 음악'이라는 흐름과 반대

❌ ③ unattractive는 소유 없이 이용해서 '매력적'이라는 문맥과 반대

✅ ④ attractive(매력적인)+limitless(무제한의)+explore(탐색하다) ← 정답
det.tip: attractive to them(그들에게 매력적인), limitless music(무제한 음악), explore styles(스타일을 탐색하다)

questions.passage: Related to the concern of overconsumption is the financial burden that subscriptions can create. While the cost of individual subscriptions may seem (A)[affordable / expensive], subscribing to multiple services can add up quickly. It is important to (B)[carefully / carelessly] consider the costs of these subscriptions to avoid financial strain. Regularly reviewing and canceling unnecessary subscriptions can be (C)[beneficial / harmful].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① affordable(감당할 만한)+carefully(신중하게)+beneficial(유익한) ← 정답

❌ ② expensive(비싼)는 '개별 구독은 감당할 만해 보인다'는 문맥과 반대

❌ ③ carelessly(부주의하게)는 비용을 '신중히' 따져야 한다는 흐름과 반대

❌ ④ 세 단어 모두 문맥과 반대
det.tip: may seem affordable(감당할 만해 보이는), carefully consider(신중히 따지다), can be beneficial(유익할 수 있는)

questions.passage: Limitations of the subscription economy Although the subscription economy offers many advantages, there are also some ①<u>disadvantages</u> to consider.  One concern is the potential for overconsumption.  The convenience and ②<u>accessibility</u> of the subscription model make it easy for consumers to sign up for multiple services and use a lot of content or products.  This can result in ③<u>minimal</u> consumption and using more subscription services than actually needed.  It is ④<u>crucial</u> to subscribe only to services that are truly necessary and avoid subscribing to similar services.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ minimal → excessive: 과소비를 다루므로 '지나친(excessive) 소비'가 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① disadvantages(단점): 장점과 함께 단점도 있다는 문맥으로 적절

✅ ② accessibility(접근성): 구독 모델의 편리함과 접근성을 말하는 문맥으로 적절

❌ ③ minimal(최소한의) → excessive(지나친) ← 정답

✅ ④ crucial(중요한): 꼭 필요한 것만 구독하는 게 중요하다는 문맥으로 적절
det.tip: excessive consumption(지나친 소비) ↔ minimal(최소한의)

questions.passage: Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers.  Moreover, consumers value ①<u>diversity</u> and customization.  The subscription economy offers a diverse range of subscription options, enabling individuals to ②<u>personalize</u> their experiences based on their own preferences and interests.  This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their ③<u>conformity</u> and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes.  A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service.  It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing ④<u>specialized</u> recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ conformity → uniqueness: 자신의 '개성(uniqueness)'을 표현한다는 문맥이 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① diversity(다양성): 소비자가 다양성을 중시한다는 문맥으로 적절

✅ ② personalize(개인화하다): 경험을 개인화한다는 문맥으로 적절

❌ ③ conformity(순응) → uniqueness(개성) ← 정답

✅ ④ specialized(전문화된): 맞춤 추천을 제공한다는 문맥으로 적절
det.tip: expressing their uniqueness(개성 표현) ↔ conformity(순응)

questions.passage: Online platforms drive the subscription economy With the development of various digital devices centered on smartphones, consumers have been able to do ①<u>numerous</u> things with great ease.  In the past, people had no choice but to go to the theater or purchase the videos they wanted to watch.  Today, whoever wants to watch a movie can access online media subscription platforms and enjoy a ②<u>tiny</u> selection of movies on their smartphones or other digital devices.  At the same time, these platforms make it easy for companies to offer ③<u>customized</u> products and services to customers.  By applying AI and big data algorithm technology, companies ④<u>identify</u> consumers’ needs, tastes, and consumption patterns.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② tiny → vast: 스마트폰으로 '방대한(vast)' 영화를 즐긴다는 문맥이 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① numerous(수많은): 수많은 일을 쉽게 할 수 있다는 문맥으로 적절

❌ ② tiny(아주 작은) → vast(방대한) ← 정답

✅ ③ customized(맞춤형의): 기업이 맞춤 상품을 제공한다는 문맥으로 적절

✅ ④ identify(파악하다): AI로 소비자 needs를 파악한다는 문맥으로 적절
det.tip: a vast selection(방대한 선택) ↔ tiny(아주 작은)

questions.passage: The subscription economy brings advantages for both companies and consumers.  Companies can have a stable revenue and build customer __________ by using the subscription model.  From the consumers’ perspective, they can enjoy a wider range of choices and personalized experiences.  They can also save money by having flexible subscription contracts.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① pollution(오염): 기업의 이점 문맥과 무관

✅ ② loyalty(충성도): 구독 모델로 고객 충성도를 쌓는다 ← 정답

❌ ③ ownership(소유): 이 문장의 흐름과 맞지 않음

❌ ④ strain(부담): 부정적 의미라 문맥과 반대
det.tip: build customer loyalty: 고객 충성도를 쌓다

questions.passage: It is important to carefully consider the costs of these subscriptions to avoid financial strain.  Regularly reviewing and canceling unnecessary subscriptions can be beneficial.  Additionally, the subscription economy can contribute to environmental __________.  The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can increase the use of disposable packaging, which harms the environment.  Using environmentally friendly packaging materials and opting for reusable packaging can help reduce this problem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① flexibility(유연성): 뒤에 이어지는 포장재·환경 피해와 무관

❌ ② convenience(편리함): 긍정적 의미라 문맥과 반대

✅ ③ pollution(오염): 일회용 포장이 환경에 해를 끼친다는 문맥 ← 정답

❌ ④ satisfaction(만족): 부정적 결과를 다루는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: contribute to environmental pollution: 환경 오염에 기여하다

questions.passage: More and more people prioritize experiences over owning things.  This makes the subscription economy attractive to them because it offers access to services or content without the requirement of __________.  For example, by subscribing to a music streaming service, consumers can enjoy limitless music without the need for having disc albums.  Another example is subscribing to clothing services, where consumers can explore a variety of clothing styles without filling up their drawers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① ownership(소유): 소유의 요건 없이 서비스에 접근한다 ← 정답

❌ ② albums(앨범): 뒤 예시에 나오지만 이 빈칸의 상위 개념이 아님

❌ ③ attention(관심): 문맥과 무관

❌ ④ comfort(편안함): 이 문장의 핵심이 아님
det.tip: without the requirement of ownership: 소유의 요건 없이

questions.passage: After school, Jiyun <u>utilizes</u> a video lecture service to expand her knowledge in whatever she finds interesting.  For example, she watches various academic lectures to review her schoolwork and stay updated about the latest knowledge in her chosen field of study.  During weekends, Jiyun and her family spend quality time together watching movies or dramas using a streaming service.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 utilizes와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① ignores(무시하다): utilizes와 반대

✅ ② uses(이용하다): utilizes와 같은 뜻 ← 정답

❌ ③ breaks(부수다): 뜻이 다름

❌ ④ delays(미루다): 뜻이 다름
det.tip: utilizes = uses = (서비스를) 이용하다, 활용하다

questions.passage: Initially it was limited to products such as milk and newspapers.  However, these business models have expanded to all industries, including entertainment, technology, fashion, education, and much more.  Instead of creating a hit product that will be sold once, companies now <u>prioritize</u> providing continuing value, such as new content, more personalization, or access to updates.  Customers pay for these benefits via a regular subscription.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 prioritize와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① neglect(소홀히 하다): prioritize와 반대

❌ ② postpone(미루다): 뜻이 다름

❌ ③ reveal(드러내다): 뜻이 다름

✅ ④ emphasize(중시하다): prioritize와 가까운 뜻 ← 정답
det.tip: prioritize = emphasize = 우선시하다, 중시하다

questions.passage: In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed.  This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only what they really need.  Moreover, subscription services are made easily <u>accessible</u> by online platforms, enhancing consumers’ convenience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 accessible과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① expensive(비싼): 뜻이 다름

❌ ② hidden(숨겨진): accessible과 반대

✅ ③ available(이용 가능한): accessible과 가까운 뜻 ← 정답

❌ ④ limited(제한된): 접근성과 반대되는 의미
det.tip: made easily accessible = 쉽게 이용 가능하게 만든

questions.passage: Moreover, consumers value diversity and customization.  The subscription economy offers a <u>diverse</u> range of subscription options, enabling individuals to personalize their experiences based on their own preferences and interests.  This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy expressing their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes.  A popular example that has gained attention is the cosmetics subscription service.  It stands out by thoroughly analyzing customers’ current skin conditions and providing specialized recommendations, including manufacturing cosmetics created to address each individual’s unique skin concerns.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 diverse와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① varied(다양한): diverse와 비슷한 뜻이라 반의어 아님

✅ ② uniform(획일적인): diverse와 반대 ← 정답 (본문 뒤 uniform purchasing process와 연결)

❌ ③ modern(현대의): 의미축이 다름

❌ ④ frequent(잦은): 빈도와 관련되어 의미축이 다름
det.tip: diverse(다양한) ↔ uniform(획일적인)

questions.passage: Additionally, the subscription economy can contribute to environmental pollution.  The regular delivery of products in packaging materials can <u>increase</u> the use of disposable packaging, which harms the environment.  Using environmentally friendly packaging materials and opting for reusable packaging can help reduce this problem.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 increase와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① expand(늘리다): increase와 비슷한 뜻이라 반의어 아님

❌ ② deliver(배달하다): 의미축이 다름

❌ ③ harm(해치다): 의미축이 다름

✅ ④ reduce(줄이다): increase와 반대 ← 정답 (본문 뒤 help reduce this problem과 연결)
det.tip: increase(늘리다) ↔ reduce(줄이다)

questions.passage:
(A) Companies now prioritize providing continuing <u>value</u>, such as new content and access to updates, so customers keep paying every month. This kind of worth is what makes the subscription model attractive.
(B) More and more young consumers <u>value</u> diversity and customization. They are willing to spend time and money on services that fit their own tastes.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 value의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) continuing value = 지속적인 '가치'(명사), (B) value diversity = 다양성을 '소중히 여기다'(동사) ← 정답

❌ ② (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜

❌ ③ (A)는 '가격'이 아니라 '가치'

❌ ④ (B)는 '평가하다'가 아니라 '소중히 여기다'
det.tip: value: (A) 가치(worth, 명사) / (B) 소중히 여기다(to think important, 동사)

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the quality of being easy to use or do without much effort or trouble"

det.analysis:
❌ ① pollution(오염): 환경 피해를 뜻함

❌ ② loyalty(충성도): 꾸준히 이용하는 마음을 뜻함

✅ ③ convenience(편리함): 큰 노력 없이 쉽게 할 수 있는 성질 ← 정답

❌ ④ strain(부담): 압박이나 긴장을 뜻함
det.tip: convenience = 큰 수고 없이 쉽게 쓰거나 할 수 있는 성질(편리함)

questions.passage: This aspect of the subscription economy is more popular among younger generations, as they enjoy __________ (express) their uniqueness and discovering valuable content and services that fit with their individual tastes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: express(원형) → expressing: 동사 enjoy는 목적어로 동명사(-ing)를 취한다. 뒤의 discovering과 and로 나란히 연결되는 병렬 구조라서, 앞도 -ing 형태인 expressing이 되어야 한다.
det.tip: enjoy + 동명사(-ing): enjoy expressing (표현하는 것을 즐기다)

questions.passage: Despite the potential limitations of subscription services, they have become deeply __________ (embed) in our lives and more and more businesses are jumping onto the subscription economy model.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: embed(원형) → embedded: 'have become + 과거분사' 형태로, 구독 서비스가 우리 삶에 '깊이 자리 잡게 된' 수동·완료의 상태를 나타낸다. embed는 짧은 모음 뒤 자음 b를 하나 더 겹쳐 -bed로 만든다(embedded).
det.tip: become + 과거분사(deeply embedded): 깊이 자리 잡게 되다

questions.passage: Furthermore, consumers appreciate flexibility and convenience.  In some subscription models, consumers can experience a variety of products or services for a fixed cost.  In other models, they can flexibly adjust subscription fees by choosing only the necessary services or products when needed.  This means they can either enjoy a range of offerings for a set price or save money by selecting only __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 what they really need(정말로 필요한 것)가 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① what they really need(정말로 필요한 것): 필요한 것만 골라 돈을 아낀다 ← 정답

❌ ② how much they can spend(얼마나 쓸 수 있는지): 선택 기준이 아니라 예산 이야기라 어색

❌ ③ when the price rises(가격이 오를 때): 흐름과 무관

❌ ④ who the seller is(판매자가 누구인지): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: save money by selecting only what they really need: 정말 필요한 것만 골라 돈을 아끼다

questions.passage: Limitations of the subscription economy Although the subscription economy offers many advantages, there are also some disadvantages to consider.  One concern is the potential for overconsumption.  The convenience and accessibility of the subscription model make it easy for consumers to sign up for multiple services and use a lot of content or products.  This can result in excessive consumption and using __________.  It is crucial to subscribe only to services that are truly necessary and avoid subscribing to similar services.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 more subscription services than actually needed(실제 필요한 것보다 많은 구독 서비스)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① the same content as before(이전과 같은 콘텐츠): 과소비 문맥과 무관

❌ ② only the services that are free(무료 서비스만): 과소비와 반대

❌ ③ fewer devices than they can afford(감당할 수 있는 것보다 적은 기기): 과소비와 반대

✅ ④ more subscription services than actually needed(필요 이상으로 많은 구독): 과소비의 위험을 설명 ← 정답
det.tip: excessive consumption = using more subscription services than actually needed
